1. AlphaONERYAV
In development

AlphaONE

One box for flight instruments, engine data, traffic and navigation, with an iPad as the display.

  • AHRS on its own microcontroller, with two IMUs and automatic switchover if one fails
  • Pitot and static inputs for airspeed, altitude and vertical speed
  • ADS-B In from open-source Stratux code, plus GPS and flight logging
  • Works with Adventure Pilot’s-IFLYEFB for course guidance and controls Garmin radios and a Garmin transponder
  • External three-hour backup battery pack, and open source throughout
2. Autopilot control headRYAV
Planned for AlphaONE Rev 2

Autopilot control head

An autopilot computer in a panel-mounted head, linked to AlphaONE over CAN.

  • Keys and a display for mode selection, modeled on a Garmin-style mode controller
  • A pitch wheel, a heading knob and a separate altitude knob, so each target has its own control
  • Planned modes: level, heading, track, navigation, altitude, vertical speed and airspeed
  • Clutched servo built for flaperon control
  • The stick disconnect switch cuts clutch power in hardware, with no software in the path
3. EMS-4N596JW
V1.0, operator's manual Rev A

EMS-4 engine monitor

Engine monitoring configured for the Rotax 912 ULS.

  • 20×4 character display on an ATmega2560 main board
  • Sends GRT EIS-format data to an iLevil 3 AW over RS-232
  • Demonstrator aircraft: N596JW, a Kitfox with a Rotax 582
4. UAT transmitterRYAV
In design

978 MHz UAT transmitter

A broadcast-only ADS-B Out unit that works alongside AlphaONE.

  • Transmits only; ADS-B In stays in AlphaONE
  • A separate unit, so it can be registered with the FCC on its own
  • FCC registration is planned
5. iPad appRYAV
In development

RYAV Avionics for iPad

The display for AlphaONE, with six screens: Flight, Traffic, Engine, Radios, Logs and Setup.

  • Native SwiftUI app, iPad only
  • Radios and transponder across the top, engine strip on the left
  • Live data fails over from AlphaONE to a Stratux to the iPad's own sensors
